h.select_rule: Reject any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own value or makes the edit inert, and reject any that restates a main effect. Keep 10 with distinct mechanisms, no repeated condition setting more than twice, both directions, and the most surprising yet mechanistically defensible claims.
h.strategy: Generate widely, then let selection prune. Each hypothesis must couple two different fields: the condition should change HOW the edit works, not whether the edited part is used at all. Draw on the negated default assumptions, for example that a stronger setting is always better, that effects are additive, or that more paths always help. Propose cases of saturation when an equivalent capacity already exists elsewhere, compensation where one part masks another's weakness, and reversals where a usually beneficial edit hurts under a specific configuration. Do not explain a hypothesis by saying an edit is inert, or by saying that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one. In each 'why', state the mechanism concisely and say what observation would refute it.

hyps.why: With edge 5 removed, node 2 is a dead end and the skip is the only residual route into the output; refuted if the skip gain is equal or smaller when edge 5 is none.
A 3x3 conv on edge 4 already gives the output a conv-processed view of node 1, so a second 3x3 on edge 3 is redundant; refuted if the gain is equal or larger.
A direct skip to the output stabilizes gradients so the deeper conv path can be exploited; refuted if the gain is smaller with the skip present.
With no direct edge, edge 4 and edge 5 carry all the information, and pooling blurs it; refuted if pooling is not more harmful here.
A skip on edge 5 forwards node 2 unprocessed, so pooled features pass straight to the output with no conv to repair them; refuted if the effect is not worse.
The direct skip covers the output's residual path, so dropping edge 5 costs less; refuted if the drop is equally large.
With edge 2 removed, node 1 only feeds the output, so a skip on edge 4 gives a clean second residual route; refuted if no larger gain.
Two parallel skips to the output are redundant, so the second adds little; refuted if the gain is equal or larger.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 reaches the output only via edge 2 and node 2, so that conv is the sole carrier; refuted if the gain is smaller.
The direct 3x3 conv already supplies features, so pooling on edge 5 only dilutes the sum into the output; refuted if pooling is not worse here.
